title: Symmetric Encryption
subtitle: Research / Cryptography
summary: Efficient encryption, authentication, and integrity verification for business systems.

sections.title: What we have
sections.intro: Symmetric cryptography secures information with shared secret keys. It supports high-volume message authentication, integrity verification, and efficient bulk encryption.
points: HMAC-SHA256 authenticates messages and identity-bound tokens.
Authenticated encryption such as AES-GCM protects stored and transmitted data.
Nonce tracking and key rotation provide credential lifecycle controls.

sections.title: How it works
sections.intro: Trusted systems establish a shared key. The sender creates an authentication tag for a message; the receiver checks the tag using that same key.
points: The message and authenticated fields are bound together.
A unique nonce can make an authentication token single-use.

sections.title: Business applications
sections.intro: The same efficient cryptographic operations support diverse business systems.

sections.title: Business value
sections.intro: Efficient verification and data protection help businesses secure more operations with less processing overhead.
points: Faster verification in trusted service environments
Reduced hardware and energy requirements on constrained devices
Tamper detection for messages and business records

sections.title: Symmetric vs. asymmetric
sections.intro: Symmetric cryptography is especially efficient for repeated operations between systems that already share a trusted key.
points: HMAC verification is computationally lightweight compared with public-key signature verification.
Symmetric encryption is the practical method for protecting large amounts of data.
Asymmetric cryptography supports public verification and establishing keys between parties without a prior shared secret.
Many real-world systems combine asymmetric key establishment with symmetric data protection.

sections.title: Implementation capabilities
sections.intro: The documented symmetric-attestation implementation provides a concrete example of business-ready authentication mechanisms.
